Answer: C
Reason: Comparing the two radiographs, the left upper zone in the later image (Figure 2) demonstrates increased pleural thickening and parenchymal opacity compared to the earlier image (Figure 1). In a patient with chronic sarcoidosis and established fibrocystic disease, progressive apical pleural thickening is a classic radiographic sign associated with the development of an aspergilloma (mycetoma) within a pre-existing cavity.
